observations.name: Intel Vulnerability Disclosure Program on Intigriti

facts.program: Intel Vulnerability Disclosure Program on Intigriti
facts.safe_harbor: reasonable safe harbor when program terms are followed; does not authorize research involving other parties
facts.bounty_status: No bounty for Software, Firmware, Hardware, Services; first-party products show bounty eligibility No and reputation eligibility Yes
facts.scope_summary: Maintained Intel-branded products/technologies may be eligible for reporting; third-party products, IT infrastructure, pre-release products, credentials, owner-attacker/physical-access attacks and other listed categories are excluded or separately routed.
facts.activity: Intigriti page shows recent submissions through 2026-09-25

missing_verification: Exact effective date on which Intel's prior bounty-paying terms ceased and the current no-bounty VDP terms became controlling.
Whether any separate Intel incentive/bonus lane remains currently payable outside this VDP; do not infer one from stale Intel pages or historical program language.
Whether Intel should become a recurring canonical source; this observation alone does not justify adding a competing source registry entry.
observations.deduplication: No Intel item was found on current default-branch code search. Preserve as contributed source-lifecycle intelligence only; do not create a money opportunity because the controlling Intigriti program explicitly states there are no bounties.
observations.recommended_next_action: When chronology reaches this contribution, re-open Intel's Product Security Center and the Intigriti program together, preserve the then-current terms and any dated transition notice, and classify the lane as disclosure/recognition rather than paid opportunity unless a primary source explicitly restores rewards.

notes: This file preserves contributed research only and does not advance data/source_check_history.json or data/intelligence_sources.json.

Intel's own Product Security Center routes vulnerability reports to Intigriti, but some Intel wording still calls the process a Bug Bounty Program; the current Intigriti program terms control the no-bounty classification captured here.
Do not leapfrog the protected Aug. 30 morning five-record/five-registry replay gate.
No security testing was performed and no public Intel or third-party system was treated as authorization.
